forecast-period.text: A trough and cold front located about central parts of SA continue crossing the state and clear to the east from Monday morning. A cool southwesterly airstream will follow as a high pressure system drifts eastwards across the Bight early this week.
For latest warnings go to www.bom.gov.au, subscribe to RSS feeds, call 1300 659 210* or listen for warnings on relevant TV and radio broadcasts.
* Calls to 1300 numbers cost around 27.5c incl. GST, higher from mobiles or public phones.

Isolated to scattered showers and thunderstorms continue across central and eastern districts early, contracting northeast throughout the day. Showers and thunderstorms continuing in the northwest. Thunderstorms possibly severe with damaging winds in the northeast. Maximum temperatures below average in the east, grading to well below average in the west. North to northwesterly winds in the far north, ahead of south to southwesterly change extending across the state and freshening near the coast.

Isolated to scattered showers and thunderstorms about most districts. Thunderstorms about central districts possibly severe with damaging winds, large hail and heavy rain which may lead to flash flooding. Northeast to northwesterly winds, ahead of a south to southwesterly change extending across the west and the agricultural areas during the evening.

Chance of isolated light morning showers about the southern agricultural area. Isolated to scattered showers and thunderstorms about northern parts. Maximum temperatures below to well below average. South to southeasterly winds, fresh at times in the northeast and tending southwest to southerly about the southern agricultural area.

Chance of patchy morning frost in the southeast. Mostly dry in the south, with a slight chance of a light morning shower about the southern agricultural area. Isolated to scattered showers and possible thunderstorms in the north, contracting to the northeast and clearing overnight. Maximum temperatures below to well below average. East to southeasterly winds.

text.p: Mostly dry, chance of showers and thunderstorms in the far west and north later. Maximum temperatures below average. Southeast to northeasterly winds.

Cumulative rainfall totals to the end of Thursday: Broadly 5 to 10 mm across the pastoral districts, increasing 20 to 40 mm in the far north. 2 to 10 mm about the agricultural areas, with isolated higher falls of 10 to 20 mm possible. Localised falls of 40 to 50 mm are possible with severe thunderstorms.
